articles.title: Curtains for Ravindra Jadeja in ODIs? All-rounder drops out of 2027 World Cup plans
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: It is increasingly possible that Ravindra Jadeja has played his last ODI for India.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: It is increasingly possible that Ravindra Jadeja has played his last ODI for India. The veteran all-rounder was left out of the playing XI for the third match after a below-par return in the first two ODIs against the West Indies. Captain Shubman Gill maintained that Jadeja was rested not dropped, but the writing is very much on the wall for the experienced all-rounder in the format."I don’t think Jaddu bhai was dropped. We rested him because we had an opportunity today to give game time to other players. When a series is only three matches long, it becomes very difficult to give experience to players sitting outside," Gill said in the post-match press conference after India’s defeat in the third ODI in New Chandigarh.Jadeja picked up only two wickets in the first two matches and did not get an opportunity to bat. Since the 2023 ODI World Cup, Jadeja has played only 15 of the 32 ODIs India have played. He has taken 14 wickets at an average of 47.92 and an economy rate of 5.20. His bowling returns have declined sharply in recent times.Before the Guwahati ODI, Jadeja had managed only one wicket in his previous seven ODIs, although that was not entirely unexpected. Given his bowling style and recent pitch conditions, he was unlikely to regularly dismantle batting line-ups in ODIs unless conditions significantly assisted him.Since the 2025 Champions Trophy, where he was part of India’s spin quartet, Jadeja has taken only five wickets in eight matches, with his economy rate going beyond six runs per over.He is not in India’s scheme of things for the 2027 ODI World Cup. Axar and Washington were playing in the Asian Games, whereas Harsh Dubey and Shahbaz Ahmed are at the CoE because they were injured.His batting numbers do little to strengthen his case. Jadeja has not scored an ODI fifty in the last six years. Since the 2023 World Cup, he has made 149 runs in 10 innings. While Jadeja has never been viewed primarily as a batter in ODIs, his batting was an important part of his overall value to the team.In 142 ODI innings across 212 matches, Jadeja has crossed the fifty-run mark only 13 times. His principal role in the format, however, has been that of a bowler capable of controlling the run rate. At his best, he could hold up one end, complete his 10-over spell for around 45-50 runs and chip in with a wicket or two.That reliability, though, has not been as evident recently.Jadeja is now fifth in the pecking order among India’s spin-bowling all-rounders, behind Axar Patel, Washington Sundar, Harsh Dubey and Shahbaz Ahmed."He is not in India’s scheme of things for the 2027 ODI World Cup. Axar and Washington were playing in the Asian Games, whereas Harsh Dubey and Shahbaz Ahmed are at the CoE because they were injured," a source tracking the developments told TimesofIndia.com."And when it comes to the left-arm spin all-rounder option, Axar is ahead of Jadeja. Axar has more wicket-taking ability and can bat as a floater from No. 4 to No. 7 in the middle overs. By no means is he inferior when it comes to fielding," the source added.For me, Jadeja has always been a utility player. He has definitely improved as a bowler over the last six months.The numbers over the last 12 months also underline the changing pecking order. Jadeja has taken only one wicket in seven ODIs during this period, leaving him with a bowling average of more than 350. Across the six ODIs against New Zealand and South Africa, he generally did not complete his full quota of 10 overs, with the Thiruvananthapuram ODI against the West Indies being the only exception.Axar Patel, meanwhile, has produced significantly better returns. He has taken eight wickets in six ODIs over the last 12 months, with a bowling average of 30.87, better than his career average of 32.73.After the Guwahati ODI, India’s spin bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule described Jadeja as a "utility player" and said the all-rounder had improved as a bowler over the previous six months."For me, Jadeja has always been a utility player. He has definitely improved as a bowler over the last six months," Bahutule said after the Guwahati ODI.However, the numbers since the 2023 World Cup favour Axar. He has taken 21 wickets in 19 matches at an economy rate of 4.53. Axar has taken a wicket every 45 balls, while Jadeja’s strike rate in his 15 appearances is 55.2, meaning he has taken a wicket every 55 balls.Jadeja’s batting role has also largely been confined to No. 7 or 8 of late, and he does not offer a significantly different skill set from the other options in contention. Axar, his most direct competitor, has carved out a more defined role as a spin-hitter.Since the 2023 World Cup final, Axar has scored 437 runs in 18 innings at an average of 29.13, including two fifties.There had been signs earlier that Jadeja’s position in the ODI set-up could come under pressure. Last year, former chairman of selectors Ajit Agarkar suggested that India did not necessarily need Jadeja in Australian conditions, given the limited value of playing two left-arm spinners."He is very much in the plans. But there will be some competition for places. Of course, he was there in the Champions Trophy squad because we took those extra spinners with the conditions there. At the moment, we could only carry one and get some balance in the team with Washi and Kuldeep there as well. And I don’t think we are going to need more than that in Australia," Agarkar had said.South Africa, the hosts of the 2027 ODI World Cup alongside Zimbabwe and Namibia, could offer conditions that are similarly demanding for India’s spinners. With Jadeja no longer providing the same control with the ball and his batting returns not strong enough to compensate, the selectors appear to have several younger alternatives.Gill may insist that Jadeja was rested rather than dropped for the third ODI. But with Axar ahead of him, Washington Sundar offering another spin-bowling option and Harsh Dubey and Shahbaz Ahmed also in the mix, the reality is that Jadeja’s path back into India’s ODI plans is becoming increasingly difficult.The third ODI in New Chandigarh may, therefore, have been more significant for Jadeja than the Indian captain’s description of it as a rest suggests.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ECB abandons Rooney Rule in recruiting coaches for England teams
articles.summary: The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) abandons use of the Rooney Rule in hiring coaches for national teams, saying its recruitment has "evolved".
articles.body:
The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) has abandoned use of the Rooney Rule in hiring coaches for national teams, saying its recruitment has "evolved".

In 2018, the ECB committed to interviewing at least one applicant from an ethnic minority background for all coaching roles in the national men's, women's and disabled teams.

The commitment came five years before a report from the Independent Commission for Equity in Cricket (ICEC) concluded discrimination was "widespread" in the sport in England and Wales.

Since then, the ECB has repeatedly stated its aim for cricket to become "the most inclusive sport in the country".

Asked by BBC Sport about the hiring process for 16 roles connected to the England men's and women's teams since 2024, the ECB confirmed that not all appointments were made with the application of the Rooney Rule - and it is no longer routinely used in coaching recruitment.

The Rooney Rule was implemented in American football's NFL in 2003.

Named after NFL diversity committee chairman Dan Rooney, it requires clubs in American football to interview at least one ethnic minority candidate for each head coach or senior football operation vacancy.

An ECB spokesperson said: "We regularly review our recruitment practices, and our approach has evolved over the last eight years.

"Coach recruitment processes are tailored to the requirements of each role. Some appointments involve open recruitment processes, while others involve targeted searches for specialist skillsets, experience and leadership qualities. At times we recruit an individual, and at others we recruit a team."

Of the recruitments BBC Sport highlighted to the ECB, not all were coaches - some were roles of selector or director of cricket.

They included appointments made in the past week. On Monday, Richard Dawson, James Foster and Eric Simons joined the coaching staff of the men's Test team, and Michael Yardy was named as elite national batting lead.

Rew, 18, to captain England Lions in West Indies

England include red-ball game in India tour as Ashes prep

Crawley signs Kent extension after losing England deal

The ECB confirmed at least one ethnic minority candidate was part of the process when Stephen Fleming became Test head coach in July.

In April 2025, then director of women's cricket Clare Connor did not use an open recruitment process or the Rooney Rule when she named Charlotte Edwards head coach of the England women's team.

At the time, Connor told BBC Sport: "I think the Rooney Rule should be absolutely applied in all circumstances where it is deemed feasible. I don't think it's on the whim of the person recruiting or hiring.

"It is practise within the ECB across our pathway appointments and our senior appointments in England cricket that we apply the Rooney Rule."

In its statement issued to BBC Sport, the ECB continued: "In elite sport, the pool of candidates can be relatively small. As such, we use a range of approaches, including external recruitment specialists and the expertise of our internal teams, to identify the strongest possible candidates and ensure we consider coaches from a range of backgrounds.

"We remain committed to improving diversity and representation within cricket. We recognise there are differing views on the effectiveness of the Rooney Rule, and instead of applying that in every case, our experience has shown that strengthening the coaching and leadership pipeline, and increasing the number of ethnically diverse and female coaches progressing through the system, is the most effective way of securing long-term change.

"We believe that our continued commitment to the coaching pathway and development will have the greatest long-term impact on representation."

The ECB announced its intention to implement the Rooney Rule in May 2018. Almost three years later, in March 2021, the ICEC was announced in the wake of global movements such as Black Lives Matter and Me Too.

In 2023, the ICEC's report, called Holding Up a Mirror to Cricket, concluded racism, sexism, classism and elitism were rife in the game.

As part of its work to improve inclusion in cricket, the ECB has focussed on growing the number of female and ethnically diverse coaches at all levels. In 2025, the governing body funded more than 1,000 coaching bursaries, of which 22% were awarded to coaches from ethnically diverse backgrounds.

The ECB's coaching pathway has five steps - advanced and specialist are the two highest levels a coach can achieve.

Since 2021, 21% of the coaches taking the advanced level course and 19% of the coaches on the specialist course have been from ethnically diverse backgrounds.

articles.title: Why are India, Zimbabwe players wearing black armbands during 1st Women’s T20I?
articles.summary: India and Zimbabwe players wore black armbands during the first T20I between the two sides at the Shaheed Veer Narayan International Stadium in Raipur on
articles.body: India and Zimbabwe players wore black armbands during the first T20I between the two sides at the Shaheed Veer Narayan International Stadium in Raipur on Friday to honour former Zimbabwe cricketer and umpire Sarah Dambanevana, who passed away earlier this week.The players and match officials also observed a minute's silence before the start of play in her memory."The Indian Cricket Team, Zimbabwe Cricket Team and match officials are wearing black arm bands and observed a moment of silence in honour and memory of former Zimbabwe cricketer and umpire Sarah Dambanevana, following her recent passing," the BCCI said in a post on X.Dambanevana passed away following a brief illness. She represented Zimbabwe as a fast bowler before moving into umpiring, where she became one of the country's pioneering female match officials.In 2022, she became the first female umpire from Zimbabwe to join the ICC Development Umpires Panel. She received her first ICC appointment at the ICC U19 Women's T20 World Cup in January 2023.At the age of 36, she had officiated in 72 senior international matches, including 10 men's T20Is, 14 women's ODIs and 48 women's T20Is.Her last match was the T20I between Ireland and Thailand on February 1, 2026, during the ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2026 Global Qualifier in Nepal.Meanwhile, India opted to field against Zimbabwe in the first T20I of the three-match series in Raipur on Friday. The series marks the start of Smriti Mandhana's tenure as India's captain, while middle-order batter Niki Prasad is set to make her international debut.The series is also the first bilateral international contest between India and Zimbabwe.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) on Friday announced a 15-member squad for India's two-Test series against New Zealand in November.
articles.body: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) on Friday announced a 15-member squad for India's two-Test series against New Zealand in November.Jasprit Bumrah has returned to the Test squad after missing India's previous series against Sri Lanka. He was initially named in that squad but was later withdrawn due to injury.Rishabh Pant, who missed India A's tour of New Zealand after suffering an injury during the domestic Irani Trophy, has also been included, subject to fitness.Fast bowlers Akash Deep and Anshul Kamboj have been named in the squad. Akash Deep recently returned to action after recovering from a stress fracture. He last played for India during the 2025 tour of England, where he impressed. Kamboj, meanwhile, was dropped after making his debut in England last year.Kuldeep Yadav has retained his place in the squad, while left-arm spinner Manav Suthar has missed out.The first Test will begin in Wellington on November 19, four days after the five-match ODI series ends. The second Test is scheduled to start in Christchurch on November 27. The series will be important to India's chances of reaching the World Test Championship final.India have also announced two squads for the five-match ODI series against New Zealand. Shreyas Iyer will lead the team in the final two ODIs, while regular captain Shubman Gill will turn his attention to red-ball cricket ahead of the Test series.Wicket-keeper Kumar Kushagra has earned his maiden India call up with a spot in the ODI team for the last two games.Veteran Ravindra Jadeja has been left out of the ODI side.In total, India play five T20s, as many ODIs and two Test on the New Zealand tour.India’s Test squad: Shubman Gill (c), Yashasvi Jaiswal, KL Rahul (vc), Devdutt Padikkal, Rishabh Pant (wk)*, Dhruv Jurel (wk), Ravindra Jadeja, Anshul Kamboj, Jasprit Bumrah, Prasidh Krishna, Akash Deep, Sai Sudharsan, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Washington Sundar, Kuldeep Yadav, Mohammed Siraj.India’s ODI squad for the first three ODIs: Shubman Gill (c), Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Shreyas Iyer (vc), KL Rahul (wk), Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Naman Dhir, Anshul Kamboj, Gurnoor Brar, Ruturaj Gaikwad, Arshdeep Singh, Ishan Kishan (wk), Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna*, Kuldeep Yadav.India’s ODI squad for fourth and fifth ODIs: Shreyas Iyer (c), Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Tilak Varma, Ishan Kishan (wk, vc], Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Naman Dhir, Auqib Nabi, Gurnoor Brar, Ruturaj Gaikwad, Arshdeep Singh, Kumar Kushagra (wk), Mohammed Siraj, Yash Thakur, Kuldeep Yadav.India tour of New Zealand – Test series fixturesNo.Start DayDateTimeMatchVenue1Thursday19-Nov-263:30 AM IST1st TestWellington2Friday27-Nov-263:30 AM IST2nd TestChristchurchStay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Shubman Gill and I got along well': Lindblad on meeting India captain
articles.summary: Indian-origin Formula 1 driver Arvid Lindblad has praised teenage cricket star Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and spoken about his conversations with India captain
articles.body: Indian-origin Formula 1 driver Arvid Lindblad has praised teenage cricket star Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and spoken about his conversations with India captain Shubman Gill. The Racing Bulls driver met Gill at Silverstone during the 2026 Formula One season and also attended India's cricket match against England earlier this year.Lindblad described Gill as “really nice”. He said they spoke about the differences between Formula 1 and cricket and how athletes can learn from each other despite competing in different sports.Lindblad On His Conversation With GillIn an interview with NDTV, the 19-year-old was asked whether he had discussed the demands of competing at the highest level with Gill.“We spoke briefly about the differences between our sports and some of the ways he manages things," Lindblad said.He added that athletes could learn from each other, even when they compete in different sports.“One of the cool aspects of sport is that athletes can learn from each other, but we didn't have a particularly deep conversation. It was a fairly short interaction.”'He's Obviously Very Impressive': Lindblad On SooryavanshiLindblad also spoke about the rise of teenage cricket sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. He praised the youngster for performing on a big stage at such a young age.“He's obviously very impressive. It's amazing to see someone so young performing on such a big stage," Lindblad said.When asked why young athletes across different sports were making their mark so early, Lindblad pointed to improvements in technology, coaching and preparation.“Maybe it's the rajma or something!” he joked, before adding that improvements in technology, coaching and preparation were helping young athletes learn faster than ever.Praising Sooryavanshi's achievements, Lindblad said: “What Vaibhav has achieved is particularly remarkable. articles.title: Deepti Sharma, debutant Niki Prasad rescue India after top-order collapse against Zimbabwe
articles.summary: Experienced Deepti Sharma and debutant Niki Prasad helped India recover from a top-order collapse to secure a four-wicket win over Zimbabwe in the first
articles.body: Experienced Deepti Sharma and debutant Niki Prasad helped India recover from a top-order collapse to secure a four-wicket win over Zimbabwe in the first T20I in Raipur on Friday.India had to work harder than expected while chasing a target of 115, but recovered from losing four wickets for just 19 runs to reach the target with 4.2 overs to spare.Smriti Mandhana began her first match as India's full-time T20I captain with a couple of boundaries, but her dismissal triggered a collapse that left India struggling at 19 for 4 in the fourth over.Mandhana fell for one in the second over, followed by Anushka Sharma. Harmanpreet Kaur's wicket left India at 19 for 3 before Shafali Verma was dismissed at the same score, leaving the hosts in trouble inside the powerplay.Nyasha Gwanzura played a key role in the collapse, dismissing Mandhana, Anushka and Shafali with her offspin, while Michelle Mavunga sent Harmanpreet back to the pavilion. Zimbabwe, who had lost all 18 of their T20Is this year, suddenly had a chance to pull off an upset.However, Deepti and debutant Niki had other plans.Deepti scored 49 off 37 balls, while Niki made 39 off 35 as the pair put together an 82-run partnership for the fifth wicket to bring India back into the contest and put them on course for victory.Niki eventually sealed the win with a boundary, with India reaching the target with 4.2 overs to spare. It was a challenging start to her international career, with the youngster walking in when India were in deep trouble before helping guide them to victory.Earlier, Zimbabwe had reached 60 for 1 after 10 overs, with Kelis Ndhlovu looking comfortable at the crease. India’s bowlers then kept the scoring in check through the middle overs. World No. 1 N Shree Charani finished with figures of 1 for 14, while Nandani Sharma took two wickets in the final over to end with 2 for 11.Ndhlovu scored 42, while Sharne Mayers added an unbeaten 43 to help Zimbabwe finish at 114 for 5.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Under pressure and on the move: Morkel flags mental fatigue in Indian camp amid 'jam-packed' schedule
articles.summary: India's fast bowling coach Morne Morkel on Friday praised the bowlers for continuing to deliver for the team despite the “mental fatigue” caused by a
articles.body: India's fast bowling coach Morne Morkel on Friday praised the bowlers for continuing to deliver for the team despite the “mental fatigue” caused by a packed schedule.Indian cricketers have had a busy couple of months, playing several bilateral series as well as competing at the Asian Games in Japan.“I read everything that's written on social media. One thing that we sometimes forget is that mental fatigue plays a big part. We have to manage that and you have to be smart with it. If you look at this T20 side, some of the players went for the Asian Games, and then went straight into a full series now (vs the West Indies),” Morkel said on the eve of the fifth T20I in Bengaluru.“Then they had to fly off to Delhi for a presentation there (meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi) and back here in the morning. And, now, we have to get them ready for a game. So, that is the reality and these guys are also human,” he added.Morkel stressed that players need enough time to recover between matches to perform at their best.“And for me, your execution and your skills will be better when you've recovered well, when you've slept well, and once you've mentally refreshed and that is a challenge. We're going to fly now to New Zealand. It's a jam-packed schedule there as well.”With another busy schedule ahead, the former South African fast bowler urged people to be measured in their criticism of the team's bowling performances.“And that is sometimes a tricky thing. So, I've got a lot of respect for these guys, with the performances that they are at the moment producing for Team India, with the schedule we have.“You know, and that's why I sometimes think we can allow them to make a mistake and allow them to have an off game and not be on them, because of the mental load and expectation on these players,” he added.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India vs West Indies: Rain threat looms over T20I series decider in Bengaluru
articles.summary: Bengaluru: Evening showers over the past few days have kept Bengaluru drenched, and the forecast offers little respite over the weekend.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Evening showers over the past few days have kept Bengaluru drenched, and the forecast offers little respite over the weekend. That is hardly welcome news ahead of the India-West Indies T20I series decider on Saturday night, with rain threatening a contest that promises plenty of fireworks.With the high-scoring series locked at 2-2, both teams will be desperately hoping for a full game. For India, there is an added incentive: they have not lost a home bilateral T20I series since Feb 2019.The opening match saw India chase down a modest target of 172 with eight wickets to spare, but the contest has taken a different turn since. The next three matches have produced a staggering 1,403 runs in 118 overs, with the batters dominating and the bowlers struggling to keep a lid on the scoring.The second match in Ranchi was a reality check for India’s bowling attack. West Indies chased down a target of 250, exposing the vulnerability of an attack missing Jasprit Bumrah. The series has underlined how crucial both Bumrah and Hardik Pandya are to India’s T20 plans.Arshdeep Singh has delivered at key moments, notably in Indore, but the pace attack has lacked consistency. When the quicks have leaked runs in the Powerplay, the spinners have been left to contain the damage, often without success.Arshdeep, who took a blow to his bowling shoulder from a Shamar Joseph bouncer in the previous match in Hyderabad, remains a doubt. The addition of Bhuvneshwar Kumar to the squad could prove a timely boost for the hosts.The 36-year-old is no stranger to the Chinnaswamy, where he made his T20I debut against Pakistan. Although his last T20I appearance came against New Zealand in Napier in Nov 2022, he has since enjoyed considerable success with RCB in the IPL.Bowling coach Morne Morkel did not rule out Arshdeep’s participation. “He (Arshdeep) is recovering well, so I think he is definitely not ruled out and is still available. Also, I am very excited to have Bhuvneshwar back in the mix,” he said.While India’s bowling has come under scrutiny, the batting has not been without its shortcomings. articles.title: ‘We’ve sent a strong message’: Daren Sammy on West Indies’ rise ahead of India decider
articles.summary: Bengaluru: A decade ago, T20 cricket conjured images of Chris Gayle, Dwayne Bravo and Evin Lewis.
articles.body: Bengaluru: A decade ago, T20 cricket conjured images of Chris Gayle, Dwayne Bravo and Evin Lewis. Few will forget how Marlon Samuels and Carlos Brathwaite lit up the Eden Gardens as West Indies stormed to the ICC World T20 title in 2016.The road has never been easy for Caribbean cricket. The lure of franchise leagues and their lucrative pay packages has complicated the task of keeping its best players available for international duty. The players can hardly be blamed. Just before their tour of India began last month, Cricket West Indies announced a 25% cut in international players’ retainer fees and suspended this year’s men’s Super50 and women’s T20 Blaze tournaments because of a financial crunch.Against that backdrop, their 1-2 defeat in the ODI series was far from dispiriting. They have since taken the five-match T20I series to the decider. Head coach Daren Sammy, captain of the 2016 World T20-winning side, put it that it was “box-office TV stuff”.“For us, what success means may be different to the viewers,” said the former allrounder. “For us, success is progress. In spite of all the challenges that we face, if we could come here and compete against the best team in the world – the defending champs – we tick boxes that keep us in the conversation.”Sammy said the players had refused to let setbacks define them. “Before the series started, we all knew the big cuts and everything that happened. We’re still doing well and continue to be a team that brings entertainment to the world when we are doing well. It’s not because of us, it’s in spite of all the challenges that we face. The way we’ve played, we’ve sent a strong message. If we could be consistent, the players that we have in the dressing room, they go out there and give their all. When they do that, we can compete and win games against anybody in the world.”For Sammy, West Indies’ value extends beyond results. Their brand of cricket, he believes, still draws viewers and lifts spirits across the Caribbean. “The fact that we make cricket really competitive is good for viewership. articles.summary: Ravichandran Ashwin has criticised the BCCI selection committee for leaving Yashasvi Jaiswal out of India's ODI squad for the New Zealand series.
articles.body: Ravichandran Ashwin has criticised the BCCI selection committee for leaving Yashasvi Jaiswal out of India's ODI squad for the New Zealand series. The former India spinner believes Jaiswal deserved a chance in the final two matches, especially with Shubman Gill being rested.Ashwin warned that repeatedly missing out on international cricket could affect the young batter's confidence and development.Speaking on his YouTube channel, Ashwin called the decision "unfair and unfortunate". He argued that while Jaiswal may need time to prepare for the upcoming Test series, the selectors could still have included him in the last two ODIs to give him valuable match practice."If Shubman Gill is not playing the last two ODIs, then Yashasvi Jaiswal should definitely get that spot. It is very unfortunate because all of this can ruin his confidence. Now, with the way he was scoring runs..."Ashwin also pointed out that Jaiswal had not played international cricket for around four months, despite previously scoring runs consistently across formats. He said the team management should make efforts to keep a talented player involved rather than leave him without opportunities."He was a run machine. If his confidence is getting ruined, it is the job of the team management and selectors to give him an opportunity wherever possible. But he has not been getting those opportunities at all. It has not gone to him. And it is very unfair."Ashwin calls Jaiswal a precious talentAshwin suggested that the selectors could have spoken directly to Jaiswal about playing the final two ODIs, allowing him to decide whether he was ready. He acknowledged the importance of preparing for Test cricket but questioned why that should come at the cost of ODI opportunities."I agree that he needs to prepare for Test cricket. But tell me, when did Yashasvi Jaiswal last play an ODI? When did he last play a T20? When did he last play a Test match?"Jaiswal's limited ODI experience has also raised questions about India's preparations for next year's ODI World Cup in South Africa, particularly regarding the development of backup players. Ashwin stressed that the selectors and team management must take responsibility for supporting the young batter and helping him regain his rhythm."It is very unfortunate. articles.title: 'Idolised them for years': Rachin Ravindra reveals how Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma have shaped his batting
articles.summary: For Rachin Ravindra, the journey from an awe-struck youngster sharing the field with his cricketing idols to an established international allrounder has
articles.body: For Rachin Ravindra, the journey from an awe-struck youngster sharing the field with his cricketing idols to an established international allrounder has been one of learning, resilience and quiet evolution. Yet, even as the New Zealand batter continues to carve his own identity, the influence of Indian greats Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma remains etched into his game.With Kohli and Rohit set to feature in the upcoming ODI series against New Zealand, Ravindra acknowledged how the duo has inspired generations across the cricketing world. “Everyone around the world who has followed cricket will be crazy about Rohit and Virat. I certainly am, too. They have done it for such a long time, won trophies and remained consistent while creating some fantastic moments. They are two players I have idolised for years, modelled parts of my batting on and learnt little things from,” Ravindra said.For Ravindra, Kohli’s mastery in bouncy conditions and Rohit’s command against spin offer valuable lessons in adaptability, temperament and intent. “Watching the way Virat plays in bouncy conditions and the way Rohit plays spin has influenced me in several ways. Beyond technique, it is about their grit and determination. Kohli’s hundreds in challenging situations and Rohit’s free-flowing, fearless approach at the top are qualities I try to take from both. So, picking their brains a little bit over the years has been fantastic,” he said.Ravindra’s own breakthrough came during the 2023 ODI World Cup in India, where he amassed 578 runs at an average of 64.22. Kohli finished with 765 runs and Rohit with 594.The remarkable campaign brought Ravindra into cricket’s next celebrated elite. However, the 26-year-old doesn’t want to overthink such comparisons. “It is a privilege to be mentioned in that conversation, but the original Fab Four are streets ahead of us at the moment. Their records are fantastic, and they remain great players and idols of mine. Ultimately, my priority is to contribute to the team. That matters more than individual accolades or the number of runs I score,” he said.New Zealand, meanwhile, will draw confidence from their historic 3-0 Test series triumph in India last year. Ravindra believes that victory, achieved against a formidable home side, will strengthen the Black Caps’ belief.“Beating such a quality team in its own conditions gives you enormous confidence. Previous tours to India were difficult, and sometimes we were fortunate to win a session, rather than a match. To win three games against a side featuring Rohit, Virat, Ashwin and Ravindra Jadeja was a proud moment,” he said.(Watch India tour of New Zealand live and exclusive on Sony Sports Network and Sony LIV starting Oct 22, 2026)Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: India’s ODI plans for the 2027 World Cup continue to evolve, with the selectors making several changes to the squads for the upcoming five-match series
articles.body: India’s ODI plans for the 2027 World Cup continue to evolve, with the selectors making several changes to the squads for the upcoming five-match series against New Zealand. The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) on Friday announced separate squads for the first three and final two matches, with the split aimed at giving Test regulars time to prepare for the two-match red-ball series, which begins just four days after the ODIs.The selections have raised questions over the futures of some established players, with Ravindra Jadeja emerging as the biggest omission from the squad for the first three matches. The veteran allrounder has struggled for form over the past several months, and his exclusion could be a significant setback to his hopes of making India’s squad for the 2027 World Cup.Axar Patel has been brought in as a like-for-like replacement for Jadeja. The left-arm allrounder last played an ODI in July against England and will now have an opportunity to strengthen his case for a place in the team for the marquee tournament in Africa.Another notable omission is Yashasvi Jaiswal, who has been left out of both squads for the New Zealand series. The decision means the opener will miss an opportunity to partner Rohit Sharma at the top of the order after Shubman Gill leaves the ODI squad to prepare for the Tests. Gill is set to depart after the first two matches. The BCCI has not provided an explanation for Jaiswal’s exclusion.Wicketkeeper Dhruv Jurel has also been left out and replaced by Ishan Kishan, despite not getting an opportunity to play in the first four ODIs against West Indies. Kishan, along with Shreyas Iyer and Arshdeep Singh, returns to the fold after missing the West Indies series due to the 2026 Asian Games.There has also been a change in the pace department. Auqib Nabi, who featured in the first ODI against West Indies in Guwahati, conceded 84 runs without taking a wicket and has been replaced by Anshul Kamboj for the first three matches against New Zealand. The arrangement will be reversed for the final two ODIs, with Kamboj leaving for Test preparations and Nabi returning to the squad.The squad will undergo further changes after the first three ODIs, with Shubman Gill, KL Rahul, Anshul Kamboj and Prasidh Krishna leaving to focus on preparations for the Test series.Tilak Varma will join the squad for the final two matches, along with Kumar Kushagra and Yash Thakur, who are set to make their ODI debuts. articles.body: Former Sri Lanka all-rounder Chaminda Vaas is set for his maiden coaching stint in the Indian Premier League after being appointed Delhi Capitals' fast bowling coach ahead of the 2027 season.Vaas, one of Sri Lanka's most successful fast bowlers, claimed 355 wickets in Tests and 400 in ODIs during his international career. He joins a revamped Capitals coaching staff headed by former India captain Sourav Ganguly, with former India all-rounder Yuvraj Singh having been appointed assistant and batting coach earlier this week.The 52-year-old replaces former India pacer Munaf Patel, who served as Delhi's bowling coach over the previous two seasons.Vaas brings considerable international coaching experience to the role. He has worked with Sri Lanka's men's team in three separate stints and also had a brief coaching contract with New Zealand. He was appointed Sri Lanka's bowling coach from 2013 to 2015 before taking up the same role with Ireland for the 2016 T20 World Cup. He subsequently returned to the Sri Lankan set-up.The former left-arm pacer is also familiar with the IPL, having represented Deccan Chargers between 2008 and 2010. He picked up 18 wickets in 13 matches for the franchise.Vaas' appointment is the latest development in Delhi Capitals' preparations for the 2027 season, as the franchise continues to reshape its backroom staff under Ganguly's leadership.Delhi have also been active in the player trade market in recent months. Pacer T Natarajan moved back to Sunrisers Hyderabad from Delhi, with spinner Zeeshan Ansari heading in the opposite direction. Natarajan, acquired by Delhi for Rs 10.75 crore at the 2025 auction, moved to SRH at a revised fee of Rs 5 crore, while Ansari joined the Capitals at his existing fee of Rs 40 lakh.In another major trade announced months ago, wicketkeeper-batter Rishabh Pant returned to Delhi Capitals from Lucknow Super Giants, while left-arm spinner Kuldeep Yadav moved to Lucknow. articles.summary: Former Indian cricketer Abhishek Nayar stated that India would need to get Shai Hope out, as the West Indies captain has been tormenting the bowling
articles.body: Former Indian cricketer Abhishek Nayar stated that India would need to get Shai Hope out, as the West Indies captain has been tormenting the bowling attack and winning matches almost single-handedly.Hope has been in stellar form in the ongoing white-ball series against India, having scored four centuries across three ODIs and four T20Is, often proving to be the difference between the two sides.India have lost all three matches in which they failed to dismiss Hope during the ongoing white-ball series, with the batter scoring unbeaten centuries in each of them. With the T20I series locked at 2-2 ahead of Saturday's decider in Bengaluru, Nayar said the Men in Blue need to find a way to dismiss Hope and suggested strategies they could employ to remove him early."The West Indies have batted well, and in the previous match, they bowled well too. But you have to find a way to get Shai Hope out. You have to find a way to stop the West Indies from scoring runs in the powerplay, and that's where the think tank comes together, plans, makes strategies, and puts all that together; then you can get the result you desire," Nayar told JioStar.Hope has scored 539 runs in seven white-ball innings, including four centuries. His 261 runs in four T20Is are already the most by any visiting batter in a bilateral series in India, reflecting his dominance throughout the tour."After a long time, such a player has come to India, scoring runs, captaining, wicket-keeping as well, and consistently scoring runs with the bat. When he scores runs, the team wins, and that is the hallmark of a terrific and great player who scores runs and makes sure the team wins. He is using his craft and finesse as well as power, and that is one thing that Shai Hope has done brilliantly," Nayar said while praising Hope.Nayar also suggested that India should vary their lines and lengths against Hope, who has found deliveries aimed at the stumps easy to score off."When you are bowling at the stumps, it's been very easy for him to score runs, which means sometimes inconsistency is the best consistency to have against Shai Hope."That is something India will have to think about and come up with a plan as to how they are going to make sure that he starts playing more behind square and how they start using the short ball more against him," he added.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: India are set to face the West Indies in the fifth and final T20I in Bengaluru on Saturday, with the series locked at 2-2.
articles.body: India are set to face the West Indies in the fifth and final T20I in Bengaluru on Saturday, with the series locked at 2-2. Ahead of the decider, former India assistant coach Abhishek Nayar has backed Sanju Samson to carry his confidence from the previous match into the series finale, while weighing in on the possibility of including teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi in the playing XI.Speaking on JioHotstar's ‘Game Plan’, Nayar praised Samson's approach in the fourth T20I, saying the wicketkeeper-batter appeared to be back in his rhythm and could play a decisive role if he spends more time at the crease.'Dangerous Sanju was back in his rhythm'Nayar felt Samson's start in the fourth T20I was particularly encouraging, with the batter looking settled and in control at the crease."In the beginning, it was a very good strategic call, with Sanju Samson taking the strike. After that, the way he was batting, it felt like he was setting himself up for a big one because he was in control. His base was good, along with control, and his head was steady. It felt like that dangerous Sanju was back in his rhythm in the last game. He will take this confidence into Bengaluru, and I feel this Indian team will be in a much better position because a lot of the batters are in form. It's only a matter of them delivering together," Nayar said.India could not convert the promising start into a victory, but Nayar believes Samson's innings offered encouragement heading into the series decider. He also pointed out that while Abhishek Sharma was not at his best, Samson stepped up to give India the momentum they needed."Yes, Abhishek Sharma wasn't in his greatest of flows, but Sanju Samson took over. That start, even though India didn't get that result, is invaluable because you could get close. So, you want to take that confidence going forward and say, if Sanju can bat for a few more overs, then in the next game, India will be sitting pretty in making sure they win the series 3-2."Nayar tempted by Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, but favours bowling changesWith the series on the line, India could consider changes to their playing XI. However, Nayar believes the team management faces a difficult decision, particularly if it considers bringing in 15-year-old Sooryavanshi.The youngster's inclusion would raise questions about the batting order, as Nayar feels Sooryavanshi should be used as an opener rather than being asked to bat outside his strongest position."I think India are in a Catch-22 situation. I'll take a punt and try and go the Kuldeep Yadav way. So, I may replace Naman Dhir with Kuldeep Yadav and get Nitish and Axar one place up. Axar Patel has also played that role of a floater really well for Team India when he has been sent up," he said.Nayar admitted that he was keen to see Sooryavanshi feature in Bengaluru, given the conditions at the venue. However, he stressed that selecting the youngster would require a reshuffle at the top of the order, potentially affecting other batters' roles."I am very tempted to play Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. But are you going to play him out of position? If Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is playing, then he plays in his strongest position, which is opening. And if he is opening, then whoever is number three should also be playing in his strongest position. However tempted I may be to see Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, that too in Bengaluru in such good conditions, I will make changes in the bowling, not in the batting at all," Nayar added.His preferred option is to strengthen the bowling attack by bringing in Kuldeep Yadav, potentially at the expense of Naman Dhir, while moving Nitish Reddy and Axar Patel up one position. The suggestion would allow India to make a tactical adjustment without disturbing the existing batting combination.India, will have to assess the availability of Arshdeep Singh, who suffered a blow to his left shoulder during the fourth T20I in Hyderabad. Bhuvneshwar Kumar has been added to the squad, with a decision on his participation to be taken before the match based on his recovery.With the series evenly poised, India will be looking to secure a 3-2 victory on home soil, while the West Indies have an opportunity to claim a series win in India.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Arrogant and cocky': AB de Villiers on why Virat Kohli seemed 'overly confident'
articles.summary: Virat Kohli's close friendship with AB de Villiers is one of the most enduring bonds in cricket, strengthened over the years by their time together at
articles.body: Virat Kohli's close friendship with AB de Villiers is one of the most enduring bonds in cricket, strengthened over the years by their time together at Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) in the Indian Premier League (IPL). However, their relationship did not begin with the kind of admiration that defines it today, with the former South Africa captain admitting that his first impression of the Indian batting great was that he was "arrogant and cocky".Speaking on a podcast with Prakhar Gupta, De Villiers looked back at his initial perception of Kohli and explained why the young Indian had come across that way when they first met.Asked whether he had genuinely considered Kohli "arrogant and cocky", De Villiers did not deny it."Yeah, and I think he'll agree with that," he said.The South African great clarified that what he had initially interpreted as arrogance was largely Kohli's extraordinary self-belief. According to De Villiers, the Indian batter's confidence was evident from an early age, although it could sometimes be misunderstood by those around him."Just a high level of confidence and he's always played his cricket that way. It gets misinterpreted sometimes. In my case, that's what happened as well. He came across as overly confident," he said.De Villiers added that his description of Kohli was partly tongue-in-cheek, while acknowledging that the former India captain possessed immense confidence during his formative years in international cricket."I mean, that was my first impression. It's always tongue-in-cheek when I say that, but I think he'll agree with that. He was a very confident youngster at the age of 19, 20, 21. Early days. That's also what's necessary to achieve great success. You really need to believe in your own ability and you just learn to manage that over the years," he added.De Villiers also reflected on how Kohli's outlook changed as he matured, suggesting that the confidence which had once appeared excessive gradually gave way to a more balanced personality.The former South Africa captain felt Kohli's early years were shaped by a strong desire to prove himself, but that instinct softened as he established himself among the leading players in world cricket."That faded away as he grew older and as he became more balanced as a person and as a cricket player. I think he had a lot to prove when he was younger, and that faded away. And that also changed that sense of having to be overly confident with people, but that changed," he said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Why not take Indian citizenship?’: Bombay HC asks 12 OCI cardholders challenging BCCI's Indian passport rule
articles.summary: The Bombay High Court has questioned 12 young cricketers holding Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cards who have challenged the Board of Control for
articles.body: The Bombay High Court has questioned 12 young cricketers holding Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cards who have challenged the Board of Control for Cricket in India’s (BCCI) decision to make an Indian passport mandatory for participation in its tournaments. The court orally observed that those keen to represent India could consider applying for Indian citizenship.A division bench of Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna was hearing petitions filed by Kavin Kartik, Avik Dixit, Ram Repala, Ameyamanasa Reddy Pamulapati, Ayaan Mohammed Ahmed, Vedant Pathak, Nirvetla Rishith Reddy, Kothapally Kritin Reddy, Kothapally Arnav Reddy, Ritesh Sai Eswar, Aryan Singh Sidhu and Kudugunta Krithik Reddy.The bench noted that the Central government, which has been made a party to the case, had not yet filed its response. Although the court indicated that the hearing could be postponed, advocate Kunal Cheema, assisted by advocate Datta Mane, urged the judges to consider the petitions.Cheema argued that the players were seeking permission to participate only in domestic tournaments, not an immediate right to represent India internationally. Playing in these competitions would allow them to build up their performance records, which could help them qualify for the likes of Indian Premier League (IPL).He also submitted that OCI cardholders were allowed to participate in such competitions until 2023, when the BCCI introduced the restriction. According to the counsel, the petitioners are young cricketers who study and live in India, and their cases deserved consideration.The judges, however, pointed out that India already has a large pool of cricketing talent. Chief Justice Tripathi questioned whether other countries would allow foreign nationals or overseas citizens to compete in domestic sporting competitions when their own citizens were available.The bench also drew a comparison with government jobs and civil service examinations, asking whether OCI cardholders could compete for such opportunities. The Chief Justice suggested that objections from domestic players might have contributed to the BCCI’s decision.Cheema argued that the restriction created a barrier to the players’ cricketing ambitions. He said that even if they wanted to play in the IPL, they first needed domestic performances and statistics to establish their credentials. The BCCI’s rule prevented them from building that record through its tournaments.Responding on behalf of the BCCI, senior advocate Dr Birendra Saraf said the Citizenship Act did not permit OCI cardholders to represent India at the international level. He also referred to the Central government’s position that only Indian citizens could play for the country.Saraf argued that the BCCI invests in identifying, training and developing players through its domestic competitions. He cited tournaments such as the Ranji Trophy and said the petitioners could continue playing in school and college competitions, private academies and other tournaments outside the board’s jurisdiction.The BCCI’s position, he submitted, was that the players could continue pursuing cricket as a hobby but could not claim a right to earn a livelihood through competitions organised by the board.The Chief Justice reiterated that the petitioners were free to pursue education and play cricket but questioned why they insisted on participating in BCCI-run tournaments without taking Indian citizenship. The bench said the country had considerable domestic talent and that the players would have to make a choice.Saraf added that the BCCI would welcome the players if they became Indian citizens.Cheema, meanwhile, said he would place international conventions before the court at the next hearing, scheduled for November 25, to argue that children have a right to choose their citizenship and should not be compelled to change it.The bench clarified that it was not directing the petitioners to change their citizenship, but was suggesting an option in response to their request to participate in BCCI tournaments.Saraf also informed the court that some OCI cardholders had already applied for Indian citizenship and that their applications were being processed.The court directed the BCCI, the Central government and the petitioners to provide details of the status of these applications at the next hearing.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: South Africa vs Australia: Hosts welcome ​back paceman Kagiso Rabada for his first outing since IPL
articles.summary: South Africa consider several batting changes as Kagiso Rabada returns for first outing since Indian Premier League in May; Watch day one of the second Test from Gqeberha, live on Sky Sports Cricket from 8am, Sunday, with play starting at 9am
articles.body:
The hosts suffered a 214-run defeat to Australia in the first Test that ended in Durban ​on Tuesday , a setback that left their status as world Test champions looking increasingly fragile.

South Africa secured a dramatic five-wicket victory over Australia to win the World Test Championship last year ​at Lord's in London, but their qualification for the final prompted debate.

They played fewer Tests than the likes of England and India and faced what was widely regarded as an ​easier schedule in the qualifying period.

Their winning form leading up to the ⁠WTC final also masked some poor batting performances, ⁠which coach Shukri Conrad acknowledged finally caught up with them against Australia at Kingsmead, where they looked anything but world champions.

"We've been ‌heavily reliant on (captain) Temba (Bavuma) and (opener) Aiden Markram and then the lower order runs," he said after Australia exposed their batting fragility.

Several changes are expected for the second Test where Matthew Breetzke is ‌set to be given a renewed chance to open alongside Markram.

Ryan Rickelton is primed to take over as wicketkeeper from Kyle Verreynne but move down the order.

Tristan Stubbs, who batted at number five for the first Test, has been omitted, which could open the door for Marques Ackerman ⁠to make his Test debut.

South Africa will welcome ​back paceman Kagiso Rabada for his first outing since the Indian ​Premier League in May, placing considerable expectation on his shoulders despite his lengthy ​absence. That means they will drop one spinner.

Australia's selection is also keenly anticipated but ⁠with Cameron Green's return from injury likely delayed, they might resist the temptation to make any changes after such an emphatic win.

One possibility, however, is that Scott Boland is brought into the attack as ⁠Australia monitor the workloads of Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood ​and Mitchell Starc after all three bowled at least 29 overs in the first ​Test.

Persistent rain and damp conditions are forecast for Gqeberha, particularly on the opening two days, which raises the prospect of delays or a shortened ‌match at St George's Park.

South Africa XI (possible): Aiden Markram, Matthew Breetzke, David Bedingham, Temba Bavuma (c), Marques Ackerman, Ryan Rickelton (wk), Wiaan Mulder, Marco Jansen, Keshav Maharaj, Kagiso Rabada, Gerald Coetzee.

Australia XI (possible): Travis Head, Nic Maddinson, Marnus Labuschagne, Steve Smith, Matthew Renshaw, Alex Carey (wk), Beau Webster, Pat Cummins (c), Mitch Starc, Nathan Lyon, Josh Hazlewood.

Hazlewood says reverse swing may be a factor

Australia fast bowler Josh Hazlewood predicts reverse swing may be crucial to the outcome of the ‌three-Test series, where abrasive pitches are helping revive a fading art.

The art of reverse swing has faded in recent years with greener wickets and lusher outfields keeping the ​ball newer and less likely to rough up.

"The ball still looks new late in the innings if it gets that far," said Hazlewood about playing back home ​in Australia, but it is a different story on tour ⁠in South Africa.

"It's abrasive wickets. It's very ⁠hard underfoot," he explained.

"We probably got a hint of swing in the first innings and then as the game goes it ‌just deteriorates more and you get a bit more. So we knew it was crucial," he said of their success in Durban, where he returned carer-best figures of ‌6-49 in the last innings to secure Australia's triumph.

"If the wicket is hard, firm, deteriorating and not much seam movement, you're probably going to get that reverse swing," Hazlewood told a pitch-side press conference on Friday as Australia prepared for Sunday.

"You probably want ⁠the ball a bit harder and a little bit of ​reverse swing rather than a lot of reverse swing and ​the ball's soft. That's much easier to navigate as a batsman," he ​added.

Hazlewood, now 35, produced his performance in Durban after missing all of last ⁠season's Ashes series through injury.

"I just play every Test match that comes," he said of his longevity. "Could be your last one whenever. I don't think about it much.

"I think you ⁠know it was great fun last week playing ​with the same guys. Doing the work in the last innings and ​taking the 20 wickets for the game on what was a pretty flat wicket for the majority. I don't look too ‌far ahead these days."

articles.body: Australian batter Jake Fraser-McGurk produced a breathtaking display of power-hitting, smashing the fastest half-century in One-Day Cup history as South Australia posted a commanding 397/7 against Queensland at the Karen Rolton Oval in Adelaide on Saturday.The 24-year-old opener raced to his fifty in just 14 deliveries, breaking his own tournament record. He eventually scored 122 off 63 balls, hammering 10 fours and nine sixes to put South Australia in a dominant position. His effort also ranks among the joint fourth-fastest half-centuries in List A cricket, with India's Vaibhav Sooryavanshi holding the world record for the fastest fifty, off just 11 balls.Fraser-McGurk found an equally impressive partner in South Australia captain Nathan McSweeney, who registered his third List A century with a composed 106 off 103 balls. Their efforts helped the hosts finish with a formidable total in their 50 overs.Fraser-McGurk Goes on the AttackFraser-McGurk wasted little time taking control of the innings. He plundered 22 runs from Tom Straker's second over before launching an assault on Tom Whitney in the fourth, striking two sixes and a four.The Australian brought up his half-century in the sixth over with a boundary off Hayden Kerr and continued his onslaught, racing to 75 off just 22 deliveries. With the fastest List A century in sight, he briefly threatened to surpass his own record of reaching three figures in 29 balls.However, after surviving a couple of chances, Fraser-McGurk tempered his aggression before accelerating again. He smashed two consecutive sixes off Whitney and brought up his century in just 49 deliveries.His explosive knock finally ended at 122 in the 21st over when Kerr dismissed him, but the opener had already provided South Australia with a flying start.McSweeney Provides Crucial SupportWhile Fraser-McGurk supplied the fireworks, McSweeney anchored the innings with a well-paced century. The South Australia skipper struck 106 off 103 balls, reaching his third List A hundred and ensuring the hosts maintained their momentum after the opener's dismissal.Fraser-McGurk's performance also continued his remarkable record at the Karen Rolton Oval. Across six List A innings at the Adelaide venue, he has accumulated runs at an average of 68.66 and a strike rate of 204.97, including two centuries and a half-century. articles.title: 'A different kind of pride': Niki Prasad recalls special feeling of scoring winning runs on debut for India
articles.summary: Scoring the winning runs on your international debut is a moment every cricketer dreams of.
articles.body: Scoring the winning runs on your international debut is a moment every cricketer dreams of. For Niki Prasad, that dream became reality as the young batter held her nerve under pressure to help India recover from a dramatic top-order collapse and beat Zimbabwe by four wickets in the opening women’s T20I on Friday.India were staring at trouble at 19/4 while chasing a modest target of 115 at the Shaheed Veer Narayan Singh International Cricket Stadium. But Niki remained unbeaten on 39, while Deepti Sharma produced a crucial 49, as the duo stitched together an 82-run partnership off 63 balls to steer the hosts to victory in 15.4 overs and give them a 1-0 lead in the three-match series.For Niki, who was making her international debut, the victory was made even sweeter by the fact that she finished the chase with the winning boundary.“I think it’s a very good feeling. To go there and play the first match for India. It’s a great pride, plus it’s a different kind of pride to score the winning run,” she said in a video released by the BCCI on X.Staying calm when India were four downWalking in with India in a precarious position, Niki chose patience over panic. Rather than attempting to force the pace, the youngster focused on building a partnership and giving the team a stable platform for the chase.“I think I have been in this situation for a long time. So I was very calm inside. And I just wanted to make a partnership with a batter. So the run will be changed easily. And that was the mindset I had inside,” she said.Niki also credited Deepti’s aggressive batting for helping her gain confidence and gradually expand her own range of shots.“You played very well in the innings. And even after seeing you, I felt that I could also take a risk by hitting me between 2 and 3 boundaries. So I think this partnership – I think you were playing aggressively and attacking. And that gave me a lot of confidence to stay there,” she added.WPL experience helps Niki handle pressureThe 20-year-old also highlighted the role of the Women’s Premier League (WPL) and domestic tournaments in preparing her for the demands of international cricket. According to Niki, competing on bigger platforms has exposed her to high-pressure situations and helped her learn from mistakes, allowing her to approach her India debut with greater composure.“I think WPL and playing on other big platforms helped me a lot. Because I have already played in that pressure situation. And I have made all my mistakes. So coming here, I don’t feel so much pressure because of WPL and other tournaments that the BCCI does. So I think it’s a very good platform that I have got from the last 2 years,” she said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: India’s decision to leave out Kuldeep Yadav from their playing XI in the last two T20Is against West Indies has raised eyebrows, with former Australia captain Michael Clarke questioning the team management’s reluctance to make the wrist-spinner a first-choice option. Clarke believes Kuldeep’s wicket-taking ability makes him an invaluable asset, particularly in a format where teams often prioritise containing runs over dismissing opposition batters.The debate comes after India’s bowling attack struggled to contain Shai Hope and his men in the fourth T20I, with West Indies smashing their way to a formidable 247/3. India were left with a daunting chase and spent much of their innings trying to keep pace with the required run rate rather than dictating terms.Kuldeep, who returned figures of 2/33 in the series opener, was left out of the playing XI after an expensive outing in Ranchi, where he conceded 53 runs for one wicket as West Indies chased down a record target of 250. India instead opted for all-rounder Naman Dhir as their second spin option alongside Axar Patel, preferring a pace-heavy combination.'Can't believe he is not their first choice spinner'Speaking on his Beyond23 Cricket Podcast, Clarke questioned the decision to sideline Kuldeep, stressing that teams should focus on taking wickets rather than simply allowing opposition batters to accumulate runs."I have made my point clear about Kuldeep Yadav several times. I cannot believe he's not their first-choice spinner. He's a wicket-taker, and it doesn't matter the format; you are looking to bowl the opposition out. Too many captains play by the rules of the game in T20s and ODIs. They just say Let the opposition get whatever they do, and we will chase, rather than looking to bowl the opposition out," Clarke said.Naman Dhir Delivers, but Kuldeep's Absence Sparks DebateWhile Clarke questioned India's selection strategy, Naman has made a useful contribution with the ball in the series. The all-rounder has taken five wickets in four matches at an average of 22.80, providing the team with another option in the spin department.However, Kuldeep's experience and ability to break partnerships remain significant considerations. The left-arm wrist-spinner has enjoyed a productive white-ball run against West Indies, claiming 10 wickets across five matches, including seven wickets in three ODIs, with a four-wicket haul.Kuldeep Yadav's T20I NumbersKuldeep has established himself as one of India's most effective wicket-taking spinners in T20 internationals. In 56 T20Is, he has claimed 98 wickets at an average of 14.20 and an economy rate of 7.10. His tally includes three four-wicket hauls and two five-wicket hauls, with best figures of 5/17.His numbers in 2026, however, have been less dominant. articles.title: 'I don't want to look into stats': Ishan Kishan shrugs off no. 1 T20I  tag ahead of West Indies series decider
articles.summary: With a series on the line and the pressure of a high-stakes decider mounting, Ishan Kishan has made it clear that rankings will not dictate his approach.
articles.body: With a series on the line and the pressure of a high-stakes decider mounting, Ishan Kishan has made it clear that rankings will not dictate his approach. The India wicketkeeper-batter, currently the world's top-ranked T20I batter, said he would rather focus on playing his natural game and enjoying the challenge than allow statistics to shape his mindset ahead of the fifth T20I against West Indies on Saturday.With the five-match series level at 2-2, India and West Indies are set for a winner-takes-all contest at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium. However, persistent rain delayed the pre-match preparations, with neither side having begun its warm-up at the time of Kishan's interaction with the broadcasters. The match also marks the return of international cricket to Bengaluru after a two-year gap.'Don't care if I'm No. 1 or No. 100 batter'Kishan, who has enjoyed a rise to the top of the T20I batting rankings, said he was not interested in dwelling on whether he was the world's No. 1 batter or further down the list. Instead, he wants to approach every game on its own merit and avoid the expectations that come with rankings."Nah, I mean, at this early stage in my life, I don't want to look into stats where I stand, if I'm a number 1 batter or I'm a number 100 batter. It's just one game at a time you take, and you just try to play your best cricket. I personally love to keep all these stats aside because I don't want to get into any thought where I'm thinking about, okay, I am number one and I need to play in a certain way," Kishan said in a pre-match interaction with the broadcasters."It's not that, you just need to go in the middle and you need to enjoy as much as you can. And especially in these situations where it's a decider game, where pressure is there, you need to enjoy those moments, leave everything aside, and that's how we prepare here," he added.'Very much happy to be in this situation'Kishan also spoke about India's mindset heading into the series decider, describing the atmosphere within the camp as a balance between staying relaxed and recognising the importance of the occasion."No, it's like somewhere in the middle of both. But I know it's a decider game. We have not been in this situation recently, and so happy to be in this situation because always a decider match, it comes up with pressure," he said."It comes up with expectations and everything, and this is what we want when we go into bat. You don't want to be, like, in a situation where it doesn't matter so much. So very much happy to be in this situation. articles.summary: South Africa will have fast bowler Kagiso Rabada back in their side for the second Test against Australia, which begins at St George's Park on Sunday,
articles.body: South Africa will have fast bowler Kagiso Rabada back in their side for the second Test against Australia, which begins at St George's Park on Sunday, captain Temba Bavuma said.Rabada missed the first Test in Durban, where South Africa suffered a 214-run defeat, as he continued his recovery from a hamstring injury. He has since trained with the team and is now ready to return.With rain forecast for the first two days, Bavuma and Australia captain Pat Cummins said they would wait until Sunday to finalise their playing XIs. However, Bavuma indicated that Rabada was set to feature, saying the pacer was "raring to go".The South African captain also highlighted Rabada's record against Australia. The fast bowler has taken 58 wickets in 11 Tests against them at an average of 21.39. His tally includes nine wickets in South Africa's World Test Championship final win at Lord's in 2025 and 11 wickets in the corresponding match during the 2017/18 series, when South Africa bounced back after losing the opening Test in Durban."The bowlers feed massively off him," said Bavuma. "There's an aura and a lot of belief in KG (Rabada) and that rubs off on the other players."South Africa are also looking to make changes to their batting line-up after struggling with the bat in Durban. Bavuma indicated that Matthew Breetzke and uncapped batter Marques Ackerman would both play as the hosts look to spend more time at the crease."The first innings was where we fell short," he said. "To concede a lead like that on a wicket like that was rather criminal."For Australia, Cummins said Matt Renshaw was set to continue at number five after scoring 190 and 82 in Durban to earn the man-of-the-match award.Renshaw usually opens the batting in Test cricket, but Cummins praised him for accepting a different role in the team."He just said, 'yep, no worries, whatever the team needs'."Cummins also confirmed that Cameron Green was not yet ready to return after suffering an abdominal injury during last month's one-day series against South Africa. articles.body: Bhuvneshwar Kumar is back in India's T20I playing XI after four years, and the veteran pacer could hardly have asked for a more familiar setting for his return. The M Chinnaswamy Stadium, where he made his T20I debut, welcomed the Royal Challengers Bengaluru favourite with a roar as he returned to the Indian playing XI for the rain-hit fifth T20I against West Indies on Saturday.With persistent rain disrupting proceedings, the series decider has been reduced to a nine-over-per-side contest. articles.title: Manav Suthar hopes to bank on adaptability in alien conditions
articles.summary: JAIPUR: Manav Suthar’s rapid rise in red-ball cricket has been an education in adaptability.
articles.body: JAIPUR: Manav Suthar’s rapid rise in red-ball cricket has been an education in adaptability. From gripping the pronounced seam of the SG ball at home to working with the Dukes in county cricket and the Kookaburra in Sri Lanka, the 24-year-old from Rajasthan has negotiated markedly different conditions in a remarkably short span.Now, as he heads to New Zealand with the India ‘A’ squad, the young left-arm spinner faces another challenge: finding a way to be effective in the wind and on surfaces that may offer little turn.Rather than arriving with a rigid tactical blueprint for a country he has never visited, Suthar is banking on his ability to adapt on the go and keep things simple. “I have never played in New Zealand. This is my first time,” Suthar told TOI.His excitement about the India ‘A’ assignment is unmistakable. “I’m 100% looking forward to doing my best for the team. Not just in terms of my bowling, but in batting as well,” he said.That confidence is rooted in rigorous preparation and a willingness to learn in demanding conditions. His recent stint with Warwickshire, where he took 27 wickets in six County Championship matches, sharpened his tactical understanding and broadened his repertoire.“There are a lot of things I learned from county cricket,” Suthar said. “Like crease variation and speed variation. You have to figure out what the ideal speed is on that particular day, whether it is the first day of the wicket or the last day. There are just so many things that I picked up there.”Has switching between different balls and conditions accelerated his development? “100%. When you play with different variables in distinct conditions, you’re forced to adapt to those situations quickly. Switching and learning so quickly is incredibly good for any cricketer. We practice diligently for this. Like before our previous tour, we had a 10-day preparatory camp where we trained extensively. Similarly, before I went to England, I trained with local equipment. Those practice sessions were crucial,” he said.Looking back on a rapid ascent that has already yielded 23 wickets in his first three Tests, Suthar identifies this exposure as his greatest asset. “Playing matches across all these environments has given me a genuine feel for the game and that experience is what matters most,” he added.That experience should serve him well in New Zealand, where he will again work with the Kookaburra. His approach remains straightforward. “The Kookaburra seam is very good and always stays in good shape,” he said. “I just try to do the same thing for as long as possible. I focus on bowling in the same area and maintaining that good length, and that’s the main thing.”Then there is the challenge of bowling in strong crosswinds. For Suthar, it is not an entirely unfamiliar assignment. “Even when we played in the subcontinent previously, there was a lot of wind,” he said. “I think using the crease is much more important when you have to deal with a strong crosswind. The main thing I focus on in those situations is adapting to the conditions as quickly as possible.“I will stick to my natural trajectory. I cannot say right now what will help me in that particular situation. I will go there, see what the wicket is offering, and figure out the right length, seam position, and pace after bowling for a couple of days,” he said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: India registered their fastest team fifty in men's T20I cricket, reaching the milestone in just 2.5 overs against the West Indies in the fifth T20I in Bengaluru. However, persistent rain forced the series decider to be abandoned, with both teams finishing the five-match series level at 2-2.India broke their previous record of reaching 50 in three overs against the West Indies in Hyderabad earlier in 2026. Their latest feat also surpassed the team fifties of 3.1 overs against New Zealand in Guwahati, 3.2 overs against Pakistan in Nisshin and 3.3 overs against Afghanistan in Delhi.Fastest team 50s for India2.5 overs vs WI, Bengaluru, 20263 overs vs WI, Hyderabad, 20263.1 overs vs NZ, Guwahati, 20263.2 overs vs PAK, Nisshin, 20263.3 overs vs AFG, Delhi, 2026India raced to 14 in the opening over despite Abhishek's dismissal, with the over featuring five wides, a no-ball and a six.
