articles.title: Ranji Trophy: Karnataka face stern Saurashtra test as campaign hangs in balance
articles.summary: BENGALURU: Saurashtra have often been a thorn in Karnataka’s side, and their rivalry has produced its share of gripping contests.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Saurashtra have often been a thorn in Karnataka’s side, and their rivalry has produced its share of gripping contests. Last season, Saurashtra edged Karnataka on the first-innings lead in a league game. But the more painful memory is their four-wicket win in the 2022-23 Ranji Trophy semifinals at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium.The teams renew their rivalry on Sunday in their second league engagement of the season, with Karnataka already under pressure to get their campaign back on track.Saurashtra are a formidable unit, boasting a deep batting line-up and a bowling attack equally adept with pace and spin. Ravindra Jadeja’s absence may not hurt them much, given their proven bench strength.At the KSCA Alur Stadium, where Karnataka lost to Madhya Pradesh in their previous outing, stand-in skipper Shreyas Gopal and his team face a stiff challenge. Rain and overcast conditions could further complicate matters for the hosts, who will also be without key batters Devdutt Padikkal, KL Rahul and R Smaran.After conceding the first-innings lead to Andhra in their season opener, Karnataka have just one point and little margin for another slip-up. For head coach and former captain R Vinay Kumar, the challenges begin with getting the batting order right.Mayank Agarwal has had an underwhelming start to the season, managing scores of five and 18. With Rahul away on national duty, Mayank will have a new opening partner, with the choice between KV Aneesh, who has struggled for runs, and newcomer Rohan Patil. KL Shijith will be a crucial cog in the top order. Karun Nair, who struck a second-innings century in the previous match, will anchor the middle order, with Nikin Jose and Aneeshwar Gautam also in the mix.With a pace-friendly surface expected, Karnataka will look to the experience of Vidwath Kaverappa and Vyshak Vijayakumar, both returning from injuries. Manvanth Kumar and left-arm spinner Abhilash Shetty are also options, though Karnataka could opt for a lone specialist spinner in Shreyas, with Shikhar Shetty providing another spin option.Saurashtra, meanwhile, are set to field a settled side led by veteran pacer Jaydev Unadkat. Their batting line-up features seasoned campaigners Harvik Desai, Chirag Jani, Jay Gohil and Arpit Vasavada. Prerak Mankad also comes into the contest on the back of a crucial 129 against Chhattisgarh.Unadkat will have support from Chetan Sakariya and Chirag Jani in the pace department.Vinay Kumar is under no illusion about the task ahead.“They are obviously strong. Nowadays, you can't take any team lightly in domestic cricket. Anybody can come and win a game against you. We need to play our best game. Saurashtra plays hard cricket and won't give up easily. But we are also ready to take the challenge,” he said.For Karnataka to avoid another early setback, they will need contributions across the board, and the resolve to match Saurashtra’s intensity.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Chris Woakes autobiography: Former England seamer slams Rob Key over 'shabby' exit
articles.summary: Former England fast bowler Chris Woakes has described the way he was told he was no longer part of England's plans as ‘cold’ and ‘shabby’, saying managing
articles.body: Former England fast bowler Chris Woakes has described the way he was told he was no longer part of England's plans as ‘cold’ and ‘shabby’, saying managing director Rob Key could have spoken to him privately before making the announcement public.Woakes, who played 217 international matches for England across formats, including 62 Tests, made his final red-ball appearance during the fifth Test against India at The Oval in August 2025. Despite dislocating his shoulder while fielding, he came out to bat in a bid to help his team.However, the effort did not earn him a place in England's Ashes squad. Woakes subsequently announced his immediate retirement from international cricket.In his autobiography, The Wizard, Woakes reflected on how England moved on from him. While he accepted his omission from last year's Ashes squad and the end of his England contract, he was hurt by the way Key publicly announced that he was no longer in the team's plans.“Chris Woakes isn’t in our plans," Key said, adding, “at all." Looking back at the comments, Woakes wrote, as cited by The Guardian: “That final bit felt a bit cold. A bit shabby, really."Woakes stopped short of directly criticising Key, suggesting the words may not have been intended in the way they came across.“I have always got on well with Rob and maybe those words slipped out, not necessarily how he meant them. But he could have easily had that conversation first with me, rather than the press," Woakes wrote.The two have had little contact since the incident, Woakes added, while acknowledging that professional sport often leaves little room for loyalty.“We have barely spoken since. He is a busy man and moved on to different things. I am sure at some point we will discuss it. But in any walk of professional sport there isn’t much loyalty because the game moves on," Woakes added.England's Ashes campaign later ended in a 4-1 defeat to Australia.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Experienced top-order batter Fakhar Zaman believes Pakistan can end their wait for an ICC trophy at next year's 50-overs World Cup, which will be hosted
articles.body: Experienced top-order batter Fakhar Zaman believes Pakistan can end their wait for an ICC trophy at next year's 50-overs World Cup, which will be hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.Speaking to the media in Rawalpindi on Saturday, Fakhar said Pakistan's players had held detailed discussions about their failure to win an ICC title since 2017.“There is pressure on us as a team to deliver an ICC trophy, and we have had extensive discussions about ending the country's wait for a major international trophy,” he said, as quoted by news agency PTI.Pakistan last reached the final of an ICC tournament at the 2022 T20 World Cup in Australia, where they lost to England in Melbourne.Fakhar acknowledged that the team's failure to win an ICC title had disappointed fans, while pointing out that strong performances brought appreciation from the public.“It is natural (that) people are disappointed about Pakistan not being able to win an ICC title for long, and we also know that when we do well, we are showered with love and admiration,” Fakhar said.“When you perform well, people show you more love. When you do not perform well, naturally, they are disappointed. Whether senior or junior, every player tries to perform to the best of their ability and improve in their profession.”He added that winning a trophy brought a different kind of happiness compared to reaching the latter stages of a tournament.“The happiness you experience as a nation after winning a trophy is different from reaching semi-finals or finals,” he added.Fakhar said the players were serious about ending Pakistan's wait for an ICC title and hoped to bring the World Cup trophy home.“We are taking it very seriously. We will do our best, and we hope Allah helps us bring the World Cup trophy back to Pakistan,” he said.The upcoming tri-series involving England and Sri Lanka will be an important part of Pakistan's preparations, with the team looking to settle on the right combination for next year's ODI World Cup.“The idea is to start building a perfect combination for the World Cup from now, and the good thing is most of our players are going into the tri-series having played domestic cricket,” Fakhar said.He also highlighted the value of playing domestic 50-overs cricket before taking on international opposition in the format.“When you play 50-overs cricket after First-Class, it is much easier to adapt, but going from T20 to ODIs is never easy. It is encouraging that all the players have come through the season and are in very good touch,” he added.Fakhar also played down concerns over Pakistan's recent struggles in the Test series against England, which they lost 0-3, saying the two formats required different approaches.“We have discussed our plans extensively, although there are certain things we cannot discuss on camera. There have been plenty of discussions, but red-ball and white-ball cricket are very different,” he said.He added that changes within the team had given the players hope ahead of the World Cup, even as preparations continued.“There have also been significant changes in the team, so we are hopeful and excited. articles.summary: India captain Shreyas Iyer has backed young batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi to remain patient and continue working on his game despite not getting a chance to
articles.body: India captain Shreyas Iyer has backed young batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi to remain patient and continue working on his game despite not getting a chance to play in the five-match T20I series against the West Indies. The series ended in a 2-2 draw after the rain-hit fifth match in Bengaluru was abandoned.Sooryavanshi did not play in any of the five matches. His last appearance for India was in the Asian Games final against Pakistan. In eight T20Is, the youngster has scored 246 runs at a strike rate of over 186, including two half-centuries.India continued to rely on experienced openers Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma throughout the series. Samson scored 168 runs in five matches, while Abhishek added 145 runs. Both batters registered two half-centuries, making it difficult for Sooryavanshi to find a place in the playing eleven.Iyer advises Sooryavanshi to stay patientSpeaking after the fifth T20I, Iyer explained that he has been encouraging Sooryavanshi to trust his preparation and stay relaxed instead of worrying about missing out on opportunities."I just keep telling him [Vaibhav Sooryavanshi], you will get your opportunities. If you are consistent with your process, mindset a bit light and not think too much about not getting an opportunity....you have to wait sometimes. We have two fantastic openers who've been consistent throughout," the skipper said.Iyer reflects on India's performanceIyer said India could have achieved a better series result if the bowlers had performed more effectively in the second and fourth matches, when they conceded more than 240 runs. Despite the bowling struggles, he praised the team's batting and acknowledged the West Indies' strong performances."Could have been a different [series scoreline] if we had bowled well in the 2nd and 4th game. Batting has been sensational, execution we fell short. Credit where due, they batted phenomenally well. Kudos to Shai Hope; he was superb. The ability to bounce back even after a loss [among the big plusses]. We were not able to be consistent throughout, so great learning. Even today, the way we went about our batting was outstanding. Gonna be a challenging series in New Zealand now," he signed off.West Indies captain Shai Hope was named Player of the Series after scoring 261 runs in four innings, including two centuries and a half-century, at a strike rate above 190.In the rain-shortened fifth match, India scored an entertaining total after being asked to bat first. articles.summary: Bengaluru: It was meant to be a special Saturday, a series decider at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium, which was hosting international cricket after a two-year
articles.body: Bengaluru: It was meant to be a special Saturday, a series decider at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium, which was hosting international cricket after a two-year hiatus. Instead, rain had the final say, turning a high-octane contest into a nine-over shootout before bringing the curtain down on the game and the series.The weather may have won, but not before India’s batters gave the holiday crowd 48 minutes of explosive entertainment, smashing seven sixes and eight fours. With the series locked at 2-2, the rain-hit finale was an anticlimax in a contest where batters had repeatedly dominated and bowlers struggled to keep pace.India captain Shreyas Iyer rued the missed opportunities. “(The series) result could have been different if we had bowled well in the second and fourth games. Our batting was sensational but we fell short in the execution,” he said.After a wait of two hours and 15 minutes, the truncated contest finally got under way, with Ishan Kishan (30; 10b; 3x4; 2x6) leading India’s charge. With the match reduced to nine overs a side, West Indies skipper Shai Hope had little hesitation in opting to field after winning the toss. With just 54 deliveries to make an impression, the Indian batters had no time for caution; the brief was to attack from the outset.Even as a light drizzle threatened to bring the covers back on, India’s batters went after the big shots. The rain returned when the hosts were 118/5 in 7.4 overs, bringing the contest to an abrupt end.Abhishek Sharma kick-started the six-hitting spree with a crisp flick off Keemo Paul that sailed over deep midwicket. He tried to repeat the stroke off the next delivery, only for Shamar Joseph to pluck the ball at midwicket.Ishan needed little time to switch into attack mode. He flicked Romario Shepherd over fine leg for six before finding the gap through midwicket for four. The next delivery brought up the 100th six of the series, as Ishan swept the ball over fine leg and onto the roof, forcing the umpires to call for a replacement ball.Shamar brought the assault to an end by taking pace off the delivery. Ishan failed to connect and holed out to Rovman Powell at mid-on. Skipper Shreyas Iyer chipped in with a 14-ball 22, while Naman Dhir was just warming up with a blistering 24 off six balls when the rain returned.Bhuvi back where it all beganIndia made two changes to the XI, bringing in Shivam Dube and Bhuvneshwar Kumar in place of Nitish Kumar Reddy, who was ruled out due to illness, and Mayank Yadav.For the 36-year-old Bhuvneshwar, the night marked a return to familiar territory. He made his T20I debut at the same venue against Pakistan in December 2012 and returned to Indian colours after a gap of three years and 340 days, during which India played 106 T20Is.The rain, however, denied him a chance to make his return count.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Mumbai: Mumbai Indians have parted ways with head coach Mahela Jayawardene after another disappointing IPL campaign and are on the lookout for a replacement ahead of the 2027 season.The decision was reportedly taken at a review meeting in August after the five-time champions won just four of their 14 matches in IPL 2026. MI announced on Saturday that the Sri Lankan great would step down ahead of IPL 2027.Jayawardene, 49, was first appointed MI head coach ahead of IPL 2017 and held the position until 2022, overseeing three of the franchise’s five title-winning campaigns, in 2017, 2019 and 2020. He was subsequently elevated to global head of performance as MI expanded into overseas leagues, including SA20, ILT20 and MLC.After a disappointing 2024 season under Mark Boucher, Jayawardene returned as head coach ahead of IPL 2025, guiding the team to Qualifier 2. However, MI struggled in 2026, finishing ninth among 10 teams.MI’s coaching staff currently includes West Indies T20 batting great Kieron Pollard as assistant coach and former India bowling coach Paras Mhambrey as bowling coach. Jayawardene’s exit also comes amid scrutiny of captain Hardik Pandya following another underwhelming campaign.Jayawardene, who captained Sri Lanka to the 2007 World Cup final, expressed gratitude to the franchise and its owners.“Mumbai Indians has been a very special part of my journey for over a decade now. The players, coaching team, the incredible support of the owners and, above all, the fans have made this an experience I will always treasure,” he said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Unfair’ treatment of Kuldeep Yadav? Ashwin fears another benching on NZ tour
articles.summary: Chennai: Kuldeep Yadav often finds himself outside the Team India playing XI after an odd bad day in office.
articles.body: Chennai: Kuldeep Yadav often finds himself outside the Team India playing XI after an odd bad day in office. Indian spin legend Ravichandran Ashwin feels the treatment meted out to the left-arm wrist spinner is often “unfair”.“Kuldeep has produced results over the years and it is unfair to pin the blame on one bowler when conditions are against him. He hasn’t been the go-to option under this management, which is unfortunate,” Ashwin said, referring to Kuldeep being dropped after conceding 1-53 in West Indies’ chase of 250 in the second T20I in Ranchi.“With Hardik Pandya not yet back, I expect Varun Chakravarthy to get the nod ahead of Kuldeep (in New Zealand), though it will be interesting to see how he returns from his side strain,” Ashwin added.The veteran also expressed concern that India could once again gravitate towards a combination that prioritises batting depth over specialist bowling options.“If we have Ravindra Jadeja and Washington Sundar around, we might see India leave out an attacking spin option. I hope not, but that could again be the direction we take,” he said.If India opt for four frontline seamers, Ashwin believes the emphasis must be on picking genuine wicket-takers rather than compromising the attack for lower-order batting depth.(Watch India’s tour of New Zealand live and exclusive on Sony Sports Network and Sony LIV starting October 22, 2026.)Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Mumbai: India’s Test and ODI captain Shubman Gill will be the cynosure of all eyes when he returns to Ranji Trophy action for Punjab against Chhattisgarh
articles.body: Mumbai: India’s Test and ODI captain Shubman Gill will be the cynosure of all eyes when he returns to Ranji Trophy action for Punjab against Chhattisgarh at Mullanpur in New Chandigarh on Sunday.Gill missed Punjab’s opening game. He was in outstanding form during India’s 2-1 ODI series win over West Indies at home, scoring 334 runs at an average of 167.“Gill arrived in Chandigarh yesterday and will play the match. He is keen to get some red-ball practice before the tour of New Zealand, where he will miss the last two ODIs to prepare for the Tests,” a source told TOI.Delhi face GujaratDelhi, under pressure after a nine-wicket defeat to Bengal in their opener, will host Gujarat in their second Elite Group C match.Gujarat began with a 10-wicket win over Odisha and will look to build on that start. Vedant Trivedi scored a century in the opening game, while opener Aarya Desai made 94 and 37 not out. Wicketkeeper-batter Urvil Patel also impressed with 60.Meanwhile, veteran pacer Mohammed Shami, who took five wickets in Bengal’s win over Delhi at Kalyani, will look to put the disappointment of being left out of India’s Test squad for New Zealand behind him when Bengal face Services at the Palam Ground in Delhi.Shedge poses selection call for Mumbai against HimachalMumbai, already jolted by the loss of opener and new vice-captain Ayush Mhatre to a recurring hamstring injury, have been strengthened by the arrival of Suryansh Shedge for their second Ranji Trophy match against Himachal Pradesh at the Luhnu Cricket Ground in Bilaspur.Shedge recently impressed for India A in the one-day series against Australia A in Puducherry.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Kumar Kushagra’s India call-up gives Jharkhand youngsters a reason to dream
articles.summary: Kolkata: Kumar Kushagra’s maiden India call-up has given Jharkhand’s young Ranji Trophy squad another reason to believe, with coach Ratan Kumar hoping the
articles.body: Kolkata: Kumar Kushagra’s maiden India call-up has given Jharkhand’s young Ranji Trophy squad another reason to believe, with coach Ratan Kumar hoping the wicketkeeper-batter’s rise to the national side will inspire his teammates to follow suit as they prepare for a challenging away clash against Maharashtra in Pune.Kushagra, initially drafted into the India A squad as Rishabh Pant’s replacement, earned his maiden senior India selection on Friday for the last two ODIs of the New Zealand tour. While Jharkhand will miss the youngster’s services, Ratan believes his achievement can lift the team’s morale.“As a coach, I am feeling top of the world. One boy whom we have been with for 2-3 years, if he is getting a chance for India, the whole team gets a very good feeling,” Ratan told STOI from Pune, ahead of the second-round match.The coach recalled how the news reached the squad after the team arrived in Pune. Kushagra had visited Jamshedpur a few days earlier, when Ratan met him at the hotel, but there had been no discussion about a possible India selection.“When we reached here, the boys got the news. At dinner, everyone was talking about it. Someone told the team, ‘Sir, see, he has got selected.’ The selection came a bit late yesterday, but everyone was very happy,” Ratan said. “The message in the group was that he deserves the place.”For Ratan, Kushagra’s achievement could also inspire Jharkhand’s young squad, whose average age is around 24, to aim for similar honours.“The youngsters and friends get the feeling that I can also do it. Among us, if a player is playing there (for India), everyone gets that feeling inside that we too can go there. So, this is a very good sign,” he added.Jharkhand will look to carry that positivity into their second-round Ranji Trophy Group C fixture against Maharashtra at the MCA Stadium starting Sunday. The visitors began their campaign with three points against Kerala in Jamshedpur after securing a first-innings lead, while Maharashtra opened with a victory over Services at the Palam Ground in New Delhi.The batting unit delivered a strong performance in Jharkhand’s opener, with young opener Shikhar Mohan, captain Virat Singh and Aditya Singh scoring centuries. Utkarsh Singh claimed five wickets in the match, while left-arm spinner Manishi and off-spinning all-rounder Md Kounain Quraishi also made useful contributions.Jharkhand will have another option in the spin department, with experienced all-rounder Anukul Roy returning after his India A assignment. His comeback sets up healthy competition with young Quraishi for a place in the playing XI.“Whoever suits the team’s needs best will be in the eleven. According to the situation, we make players play. It depends on whose skills are needed in that particular match,” said Ratan, emphasizing that selection would be dictated by conditions and team requirements.The red-soil surface at Gahunje could offer some assistance to the pacers, bringing Sushant Mishra and Saurabh Shekhar into focus against a formidable Maharashtra batting line-up.In-form opener and skipper Prithvi Shaw and experienced batter Ankit Bawne will pose a challenge, while the hosts will be further strengthened by the return of regular captain Ruturaj Gaikwad.Ratan, meanwhile, was encouraged by Jharkhand’s all-round showing in the opening game and believes there is scope to build on that performance. “The boys just need to deliver, then definitely we will play very good cricket,” he said.Jharkhand will now look to translate that confidence into another solid performance on the road against a strong Maharashtra side buoyed by its winning start.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: PCB snubs Michael Atherton, Nasser Hussain after Imran Khan interview controversy
articles.summary: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) has named a six-member commentary panel for the men’s ODI tri-series involving Pakistan, England and Sri Lanka, scheduled
articles.body: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) has named a six-member commentary panel for the men’s ODI tri-series involving Pakistan, England and Sri Lanka, scheduled to be played from October 18 to 31, with prominent English commentators Michael Atherton and Nasser Hussain missing from the line-up.The omission comes two months after the duo interviewed Kasim and Sulaiman Khan, sons of jailed former Pakistan Prime Minister and cricket legend Imran Khan, during the Lord’s Test between England and Pakistan in August 2026. The PCB has not provided any reason for their absence from the upcoming assignment.Atherton and Hussain are among the most prominent voices in international cricket commentary and were part of the broadcast team when England last toured Pakistan for a three-match Test series in October 2024.The interview with Imran Khan’s sons, conducted by Atherton and aired by Sky Sports, lasted 18 minutes and raised concerns over the former Pakistan captain’s deteriorating health in prison. Kasim and Sulaiman alleged that the authorities were ‘blatantly trying to kill him’ through neglect and isolation.The broadcast triggered a strong reaction from the PCB, which objected to what it considered the political nature of the segment and filed a formal complaint with Sky Sports. The situation reportedly intensified to the point that the board threatened a player walkout, with Pakistan considering staying off the field for the afternoon session in protest.Sky Sports went ahead with the interview despite the pressure, although Pakistan’s state broadcaster PTV censored the segment. Atherton subsequently addressed the controversy on a podcast with Hussain, defending his involvement and saying the Pakistani state was attempting to ‘airbrush Imran almost out of existence’.For the upcoming tri-series, the commentary line-up features former Pakistan internationals Waqar Younis, Aamir Sohail, Bazid Khan and Urooj Mumtaz, alongside Sri Lanka’s Roshan Abeysinghe and England’s Mark Butcher. Zainab Abbas will serve as the presenter.Younis will join the panel from the second fixture, when Pakistan meet England at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on October 20. The tournament opens on Sunday, October 18, with Pakistan facing Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi.ODI tri-series scheduleOctober 18: Pakistan vs Sri Lanka, Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium, RawalpindiOctober 20: Pakistan vs England, Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium, RawalpindiOctober 22: Sri Lanka vs England, Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium, RawalpindiOctober 25: Pakistan vs England, Gaddafi Stadium, LahoreOctober 27: Pakistan vs Sri Lanka, Gaddafi Stadium, LahoreOctober 29: Sri Lanka vs England, Gaddafi Stadium, LahoreOctober 31: Tri-series final, Gaddafi Stadium, LahoreStay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Lifetime subscription to pressure’: Ex-India cricketer’s blunt defence of Sanju Samson
articles.summary: Former India cricketer Aakash Chopra has questioned Sanju Samson’s continued omission from the ODI squad, pointing out that the Kerala wicketkeeper-batter
articles.body: Former India cricketer Aakash Chopra has questioned Sanju Samson’s continued omission from the ODI squad, pointing out that the Kerala wicketkeeper-batter has a strong record in the format but has not been considered even for the final two matches of the series against New Zealand.Chopra noted that India have several wicketkeeper-batters available, including KL Rahul, Rishabh Pant and Dhruv Jurel, none of whom have been picked for the upcoming matches. Ishan Kishan, meanwhile, has been named vice-captain, leaving Samson out of the squad.“Sanju hasn't been kept now either. KL Rahul, Rishabh Pant, and Dhruv Jurel aren't there. Ishan Kishan has been made the vice-captain there, but Sanju isn't selected. Sanju's ODI numbers are not that bad. He did well the last time he played,” Chopra said.The former batter believes the latest snub could indicate that the selectors have already made up their minds about Samson’s future in ODI cricket.“It looked like this time it would be the case to at least give him an opportunity, but you did not. You said you would keep Kumar Kushagra, which is okay. His domestic numbers are good, but why not Sanju Samson? It means you have made up your mind about Sanju Samson from an ODI cricket perspective,” Chopra observed.Samson has scored 510 runs in 14 ODI innings at an average of 56.67. His last appearance in the format came against South Africa in Paarl in December 2023, when he struck 108 off 114 balls in India’s 78-run victory.Chopra highlights Samson’s T20I numbersChopra also turned his attention to T20Is, comparing the returns of Samson, Ishan Kishan and Abhishek Sharma across their last 20 innings. The figures, he argued, challenge the criticism directed at Samson despite his consistent run-scoring.BatterRuns50s100sAverageStrike rateSanju Samson6577-34.57183.51Ishan Kishan6253-36.76152.06Abhishek Sharma5844129.20200.00“The truth is that Sanju Samson has scored the most runs among them. Yet, he seems to have a lifetime subscription to pressure. Whenever there is a problem, pressure follows him. This keeps happening to him. Whether he scores runs or not, he is blamed for not scoring. If he isn't scoring, how can he be the highest scorer in the last 20 matches, when Ishan Kishan is the No. 1 T20I batter in the ICC rankings and Abhishek is No. 2?”Chopra’s defence of Samson comes amid repeated questions over the wicketkeeper-batter’s place in the Indian side. Samson was dropped during the UK tour after just three failures, despite being named Player of the Tournament at the T20 World Cup, at a time when the entire batting unit was struggling.Ahead of the Afghanistan T20I series, his place in the team again became a subject of debate on social media, with some of the discussion also centred on Vaibhav Sooryavanshi being left out. Samson responded by scoring half-centuries in the second and third matches of the three-game series.The scrutiny resurfaced after he was dismissed cheaply in the opening T20I against West Indies. However, Samson answered with an 82 in the second match and went on to finish as India’s second-highest run-scorer in the series.He scored 168 runs at a strike rate of 193.35, registering two half-centuries in the West Indies series. His performances have added weight to Chopra’s argument that Samson’s numbers deserve greater consideration amid the recurring questions over his place.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Sanju Samson plays with emotions': Ex-coach explains why Vaibhav Sooryavanshi will have to wait for his chance
articles.summary: Former India assistant coach Abhishek Nayar believes Sanju Samson’s ability to bounce back with a big innings after a few low scores could mean Vaibhav
articles.body: Former India assistant coach Abhishek Nayar believes Sanju Samson’s ability to bounce back with a big innings after a few low scores could mean Vaibhav Sooryavanshi will have to wait for his chance in the upcoming T20I series against New Zealand.Nayar also explained how India’s team combination, particularly the need for a left-right batting pair, could influence the selection decision.Samson’s inconsistent performances have often raised questions about his place in India’s T20I side, with Sooryavanshi seen as a possible replacement. However, Nayar believes Samson’s ability to respond to criticism with a big score makes it difficult for the team management to move on from him.“Sanju plays with everyone’s emotions because he won’t score runs for two matches, and everyone starts raising questions, ‘Vaibhav Sooryavanshi should play, Sanju Samson isn’t capitalising on his chances, how long will we wait?’ And at that very moment, he will score an 80 in no time. Sanju is that kind of player who will repeatedly give you opportunities to raise questions about him and then will play a big knock, making the most of his chances. So, there will be moments when there will be talks about his place, but Vaibhav Sooryavanshi will have to wait,” Nayar told JioStar, as quoted by news agency IANS.Nayar said the selection call would depend on more than just individual performances. He stressed that team balance and the management’s approach to selection were also important, warning that frequent changes could affect the team's culture and the development of young players.“Often, for a team’s culture, if you are a coach or a captain, it is crucial to make the right decisions. If you make haphazard decisions, the impact on Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s career is one thing, but the impact on team culture will be far greater. So, according to me, the decision will be, ‘Vaibhav, wait for your time; you will also get opportunities.’“Maybe in a series where Sanju isn’t there or is rested, he will play. But as long as there is a left-hander at number three and at the top, you will always think that a right-hander in between is necessary. So, it’s not so much about Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Sanju Samson; it’s about having that left-right combination so that a bowler like Bracewell doesn’t come and bowl out his overs in the powerplay,” Nayar added.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Brendan Taylor surpassed Andy Flower to become Zimbabwe’s highest run-scorer in One-Day Internationals (ODIs) after playing a crucial knock of 81 against Bangladesh in the opening match of the ODI tri-series in Abu Dhabi on Saturday. Taylor’s contribution, alongside Craig Ervine’s 93, helped Zimbabwe recover from an early collapse to post 271/8 before their bowlers bundled out Bangladesh for 172 in 33.4 overs, securing a 99-run victory.Taylor, 40, reached the milestone with his 81 off 101 deliveries, which included 10 fours. He took his career tally to 6,837 runs in 211 ODIs, moving past Flower’s previous record of 6,786 runs in 213 matches. Taylor’s record-breaking innings also marked his first ODI half-century in six years.Taskin Ahmed rocks Zimbabwe's top orderZimbabwe, after winning the toss and electing to bat, endured a disastrous start as Bangladesh pacer Taskin Ahmed dismantled the top order. Taskin dismissed Brian Bennett, Ben Curran and debutant Tafadzwa Tsiga to reduce Zimbabwe to 24/3 inside the first seven overs.Taylor and Ervine then joined forces to revive the innings, putting together a 150-run partnership for the fourth wicket. The experienced pair countered Bangladesh’s bowling attack with a composed display, rebuilding the innings and shifting the momentum back in Zimbabwe’s favour.Taylor eventually departed for 81 after being dismissed by Saif Hassan, while Ervine continued to anchor the innings. The Zimbabwe captain narrowly missed out on a century, scoring 93 off 106 balls with nine boundaries before Shoriful Islam sent him back to the pavilion.After the partnership was broken, Bangladesh struck at regular intervals to prevent Zimbabwe from accelerating significantly. However, late contributions from Newman Nyamhuri (21 not out) and Wellington Masakadza (21 not out) lifted Zimbabwe to 271/8 in their allotted 50 overs.Taskin finished with figures of 3/44, while Shoriful claimed two wickets for 47 runs.Zimbabwe bowlers dismantle Bangladesh's chaseChasing 272 for victory, Bangladesh made a brisk start through Tanzid Hasan, who scored 46 off 38 deliveries, including nine fours and a six. However, Zimbabwe struck back after removing Soumya Sarkar, before Newman Nyamhuri dismissed Tanzid to halt the visitors' early momentum.Bangladesh’s innings subsequently unravelled as Zimbabwe’s bowlers exploited the conditions and applied sustained pressure. Brad Evans led the attack with four wickets for 45 runs, while Wellington Masakadza claimed 2/18. Sikandar Raza and the other bowlers chipped in with crucial breakthroughs as Bangladesh struggled to build partnerships.The visitors were eventually bowled out for 172 in 33.4 overs, falling 99 runs short of the target. Zimbabwe’s disciplined bowling performance ensured a comprehensive victory in the tri-series opener, with Craig Ervine named Player of the Match for his 93-run knock.Taylor moves ahead of Andy FlowerTaylor’s latest achievement places him at the top of Zimbabwe’s all-time ODI run-scoring list, ahead of one of the country’s most celebrated cricketers, Andy Flower.Taylor made his ODI debut in 2004 and has scored 6,837 runs in 211 matches at an average of 35.24. His tally includes 11 centuries and 40 half-centuries, with a highest score of 145 not out. Flower finished his ODI career with 6,786 runs in 213 matches, including four centuries and 55 half-centuries.Taylor returned to international cricket in 2025 after reversing his retirement decision.
